examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Altitude of a Triangle Given Its Vertices
examples.problem: Calculate the length of the altitude $CH$ of the $\bigtriangleup\!ABC$ if $A(-1,1,0),$ $B(1,1,2),$ $C(1,-1,1).$
examples.worked_solution:
Note that the length of the altitude (height) can be related to the area of the triangle as follows:

$$
A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{b \cdot h}{2},
$$

 
where $b$ is a base and $h$ is the corresponding altitude of the triangle.

For the $\bigtriangleup\!ABC,$ we have $h=CH,$ and $b=AB.$ So, we have

$$
A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2} CH \cdot AB.
$$

So, to find $CH,$ we first find $A_{\bigtriangleup}.$ To start, we find the vectors $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(i+j+2k)-(-i+j) \\  & =2i+2k \\  & =⟨2,0,2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(i-j+k)-(-i+j) \\  & =2i-2j+k \\  & =⟨2,-2,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(0\cdot 1-2\cdot (-2))i-(2\cdot 1-2\cdot 2)j+(2\cdot (-2)-0\cdot 2)k \\  & =4i+2j-4k \\  & =⟨4,2,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC}| \\  & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $\bigtriangleup\!ABC$ is

$$
A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2}A = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 6 = 3.
$$

Let's also compute $AB$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =|\overset{\to }{AB}| \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{8} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula $A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2} CH \cdot AB,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot 2\sqrt{2} \\ 3 & =CH\cdot \sqrt{2} \\ CH & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} \\ CH & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Calculate the area of the $△\,FGH$, if $F(1,1,2)$, $G(2,2,3)$, $H(1,0,1).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{FG}$ and $\overset{\to }{FH}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{FG} & =g-f \\  & =(2i+2j+3k)-(i+j+2k) \\  & =i+j+k \\  & =⟨1,1,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{FH} & =h-f \\  & =(i+k)-(i+j+2k) \\  & =-j-k \\  & =⟨0,-1,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula to compute the cross product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{FG}\times \overset{\to }{FH} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(1\cdot (-1)-(-1)\cdot 1)i-(1\cdot (-1)-0\cdot 1)j+(1\cdot (-1)-0\cdot 1)k \\  & =j-k \\  & =⟨0,1,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{FG}$ and $\overset{\to }{FH}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{FG}\times \overset{\to }{FH}| \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,FGH$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$
